name: Technical University of Denmark
about: DTU is Denmark's main technical university, on a large purpose-built campus in Kongens Lyngby about 15 km north of central Copenhagen. Almost all of its teaching is engineering and natural science, and its undergraduate degrees are mostly taught in Danish. For an IB student the practical point is that DTU has exactly one full English-taught bachelor's degree, General Engineering, where roughly 60 per cent of the students come from outside Denmark.
ibNotes: "IB Diploma with at least 24 points qualifies for admission to both bachelor's in engineering and Bachelor of Sciences programmes."
IB Course Results / certificates are accepted only with at least 18 points, grade 3 in all subjects and three subjects at Higher Level.
"DTU only accepts IB retakes if the original exam was not passed."
If you sit the IB in the same year you apply, you must give DTU permission to receive your diploma through the IB's online database.
IB holders are exempt from DTU's separate English test, but other international applicants are not: meeting English B through your school subjects does not by itself exempt you.
quotaNotes: Quota 1 is a pure GPA ranking and is open to IB holders as well as to Danish, Nordic and EU/EEA school leavers. Quota 2 is for applicants with a school-leaving exam from outside the EU/EEA, or for anyone who thinks their GPA is too low for quota 1; EU/EEA and IB applicants who apply in quota 2 are automatically also assessed in quota 1. DTU says the quota 1 cut-off "is the GPA of the last applicant admitted through Quota 1, and it is not known until the admission process is completed on July 28th", so no cut-off is published in advance.

deadlines.label: Application (IB holders, quota 1 and quota 2)
deadlines.notes: Applies to all IB applicants, all international applicants (EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA), quota 2 applicants and exemption requests. Non-EU/EEA applicants must also have paid the application fee by this date.

deadlines.label: Documentation upload for quota 2 assessment
deadlines.notes: Extra documentation used in the quota 2 assessment must be uploaded by this date.

deadlines.label: Quota 1 deadline (Danish qualifying exam only) and final grades
deadlines.notes: Only for applicants with a Danish qualifying exam; also the deadline for submitting final grades and diploma.

deadlines.label: Admission offers published
deadlines.notes: Offers are released through UnistartDTU; the reply deadline is 3 August.

tuitionNonEu: EUR 15,000 per year (EUR 7,500 per semester); DTU states it offers no tuition waivers or funding at undergraduate level

sources.title: DTU – Admission requirements, BSc General Engineering

notes: DTU states: "DTU currently offers one English-taught full degree BSc programme in General Engineering. All other undergraduate programmes are taught in Danish, but we offer a wide range of individual courses in English."

The Danish-taught undergraduate degrees come in two families: BSc Eng (civilingeniør, a 3-year academic bachelor) and BEng (diplomingeniør, a 3.5-year professional engineering degree, many of them taught at DTU's Ballerup campus). Both require Danish A and are described only on DTU's Danish-language site, so they are not listed here.
No published quota 1 cut-off exists for General Engineering. DTU explains the cut-off only becomes known when admission closes on 28 July each year.
DTU does not publish an IB results-service (IBIS) institution code on its English admission pages; instead it asks IB applicants to authorise release of the diploma through the IB's online database.

programmes.name: General Engineering
programmes.summary: A broad engineering degree that starts with heavy maths, physics and chemistry and then narrows into one of four specialisations: Living Systems, Advanced Materials, Cyber Systems or Future Energy. Year one introduces at least two of the specialisations through design-build projects, and the third year leaves room for a semester abroad or an industry project. About 60 per cent of the students are international, so it suits you if you want an engineering degree in English without having to pick your exact branch at 17.
programmes.requirementsText: Mathematics A-level, English B-level, Physics B-level, Chemistry B-level
extraRequirements: Documented English proficiency (IELTS Academic 6.5, Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 180, or TOEFL iBT 88). IB diploma holders and native speakers from the listed countries are exempt.
Non-EU/EEA applicants must pay an application fee by 15 March.
